pairs.why: Same rocket, but B sits on a smooth, saturated colored floor like the real cards, while A's gritty concrete tiles add the kind of surface texture the lessons marked as too texture-y.
A has the clean, smooth blue floor that matches the real cards' soft colored surfaces, while B's textured grey concrete looks more realistic and busy.
B's hull has softer, more even shading like the real submarine, while A has a streaky brushed-metal glare that reads glossier and more photoreal.
A's hull is evenly shaded and soft like the real cards, while B has a bright brushed-metal streak that pushes it toward a glossy, realistic metal look.
A's soft, glowing rock and wavy background match the real cards' smooth rendering and backdrops, while B's crisp, dark, heavily cratered rock is more texture-y.
B has the soft, smooth rock and wavy backdrop of the real cards, while A's sharply detailed grey craters read more texture-y and realistic.
B's saturated teal body matches the real cards' colorful, softly glossy objects like the blue vending machine, while A's plain grey metal on a white plinth looks more like a dull product render.
A's saturated teal body is closer to the real cards' bright, softly glossy objects, while B's flat grey metal on a plinth looks drab and realistic.
